Good morning everyone, and welcome to homeroom. A few things before the bell. If you are new this term, come and see me at the end and I will give you your locker number, because the list on the wall is already out of date. Attendance is taken here every morning at eight forty, and if you are not in the room when I call your name, it goes down as late, even if you are standing in the corridor. Two dates for you. The history assignment is due on Friday the twentieth, and if you hand it in after that you lose ten percent per day. And the field trip form has to come back signed by Wednesday, or you will spend that day in the library with me, which nobody wants.

Hey, it's Emma. Dad said you're nervous about Monday, so here's the map in words. Your first class is on the second floor, but the stairs at the north end are closed, so if you use those you'll end up outside the gym and you'll be late. Use the middle stairs. Lunch is at twelve fifteen and it is short, so if you queue at the main counter you will spend the whole break standing up. There is a smaller counter behind the library and nobody knows about it. And do not put anything in the locker before you have the combination written down somewhere. I locked my own coat in there for two days in grade nine.

Lais arrives at school and goes to the office to pick up her timetable. The homeroom teacher gives her a locker number at the end of the first class. She finds the locker and writes the combination down in her phone. At lunch she meets Emma at the small counter behind the library. In the afternoon she hands in the form for the field trip.
